text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Kabariti visits the ministry of education and stresses the importance of preparing the new generation, says government studying the setting up of a union of teachers.
- Government plans to reduce the price of bread by year-end as a result of the drop in grain prices.
- King Hussein praises the border guard patrols and their poineering role in ensuring security.
- Speaker of Parliament Srour says Jordan's abandonment of its role towards Jerusalem means allowing other non-Arab parties to fill the void.
- King Hussein receives a telephone call from U.S. Middle East peace envoy Dennis Ross who tells him that differences have narrowed between Israelis and Palestinians in peace talks.
- Kabariti gets a phone call from Kuwaiti deputy prime minister and they exchange views over the latest regional and political developments.
- Development council continues discussion over the new draft companies law.
- Twenty youths to be put on trial soon over troubles that erupted at Sports City during a soccer match this month.
- Government schools to teach Christianity as a religion.
